newsitem.title: USA: Santa Isabel founder to sell stake.
newsitem.headline: Santa Isabel founder to sell stake.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain Santa Isabel said Thursday its founder planned to sell his stake in the company for about $230 million.

The chain said Eduardo Elberg, who is also chairman of its board of directors, planned to sell his 36.96-percent stake to The Velox Group, which holds a controling interest in the Argentinian supermarket chain, Disco SA.
"The definitive terms of the purchase are expected to be finalized in the next 10 days," it said in a statement.
In light of the negotiations, Santa Isabel said it had begun a round of talks of its own with Velox.
It said it was discussing the possibility of forming a "strategic alliance" to share industry knowledge like logistics and marketing.
"(It would be) to benefit the long-term competitive position of both," it said.
"Santa Isabel and Disco would both remain completely sparate companies upon completion of the stock sale with their own existing management and corporate structures in place," it added.
The chain, based in Valparaiso, Chile, also said it was still looking to form a joint venture with an international hypermarket operator to help it develop its own hypermarket format.
